items.question: Four people talk about last weekend. What did each person do?
options: They stayed at home and watched films.
They visited their family in another town.
They went for a long walk in the countryside.
They played a sport with friends.
They cooked a meal for friends.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: The weather was lovely on Saturday, so we took some sandwiches and drove to the hills. We walked for about four hours. It was a bit tiring, but the views were beautiful, and it was so quiet.

script.speaker: man
script.text: On Sunday morning I played football with my old school friends. We do it every month. We lost three-two, but it doesn't matter. After the game we all had coffee and talked about our jobs.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: My parents live in a small town two hours away, so I went there by train on Saturday. My mum made my favourite lunch, and my brother and his children came too. It was nice to see everyone.

script.speaker: man
script.text: It rained all weekend, so I didn't go out at all. I made some popcorn, sat on the sofa and watched three old films. It was exactly what I needed after a busy week at work.

explanation.en: The first speaker went walking in the hills. The second played football with friends. The third took the train to see her parents, brother and nephews or nieces. The fourth stayed in and watched films. Nobody went shopping, and nobody cooked for friends: the third speaker's mother made lunch for the family.
explanation.es: La primera fue a caminar por las colinas. El segundo jugó al fútbol con amigos. La tercera tomó el tren para ver a su familia. El cuarto se quedó en casa viendo películas. Nadie fue de compras ni cocinó para amigos: la comida de la tercera la hizo su madre para la familia.

items.question: Four people talk about their jobs. What does each person like about their job?
options: They meet people from other countries.
They learn something new every day.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I'm a web designer. I work in my kitchen, with my cat next to me. I don't have to take a bus or a train, so I get up later and save a lot of time. I don't think I could go back to an office.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I work at a hotel near the airport. Our guests come from all over the world: Japan, Brazil, Poland. I love hearing about their countries and their food. Every day I talk to someone from a different place.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: The job isn't very well paid, and it's a long day, but I don't mind. My colleagues are great. We eat lunch together, we help each other, and on Fridays someone always brings a cake.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I drive a lorry. It's a hard job and I'm often away from home, but I earn nearly twice as much as I did in my last job. That's why I stay. My wife and I are saving for a house.

explanation.en: The web designer works at home. The hotel worker meets guests from many countries. The third speaker says the pay is low and the day is long, but the colleagues are great. The lorry driver earns nearly twice as much as before. Nobody says the working day is short, and nobody says they learn something new every day.
explanation.es: La diseñadora trabaja en casa. El del hotel conoce a huéspedes de muchos países. La tercera dice que cobra poco y que la jornada es larga, pero que sus compañeros son estupendos. El camionero gana casi el doble que antes. Nadie dice que la jornada sea corta ni que aprenda algo nuevo cada día.
